questions.q: According to the Census of India 2011, ‘Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)’ comprise how much of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 7.9 million.

Key Points

• According to the Census of India 2011, 'Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)' comprise 7.9 million people.

• The ORP category includes those who do not identify with the six major religions listed in the census data: Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism, and Jainism.

• These religions include smaller faiths and tribal religions practiced in various regions across India.

• This category helps in recognizing the diversity of beliefs and practices present in the country, reflecting the pluralistic nature of Indian society.

Additional Information

• Census of India

• The Census of India is a decennial exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, but the first complete and synchronous census was conducted in 1881.

• The census collects data on population size, distribution, and various socio-economic parameters such as literacy, employment, and housing.

• The latest census was conducted in 2011, and the next one was scheduled for 2021 but was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

• Religion Data in Census

• The religion data in the Indian Census includes information on various religious communities in the country.

• The major religions accounted for in the census are Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism, and Jainism.

• In addition to these, the census also recognizes 'Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)' and 'Religion not stated' categories.

• This data helps in understanding the religious composition and diversity of the Indian population.

• Importance of Census Data

• Census data is crucial for planning and policy-making by the government.

• It helps in the allocation of resources, development of infrastructure, and implementation of various welfare schemes.

• It also provides valuable insights for researchers and demographers studying population trends and socio-economic changes.

• Accurate census data is essential for ensuring effective governance and equitable distribution of services.

questions.q: Who among the following founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Raja Rammohun Roy.

Key Points

• Raja Rammohun Roy was a prominent social and educational reformer in India during the early 19th century.

• He founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814, which later became the Brahmo Samaj, to promote social and religious reforms.

• The Atmiya Sabha was established to fight against the social evils such as caste discrimination, and to promote monotheism and rational thinking.

• Rammohun Roy is often called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance" for his efforts to modernize Indian society.

Additional Information

• Raja Rammohun Roy:

• Born on May 22, 1772, in Radhanagar, Bengal, Rammohun Roy was a pioneer in the Indian social reform movement.

• He opposed practices such as sati (the burning of widows), child marriage, and caste discrimination, advocating for women's rights and education.

• Rammohun Roy was also instrumental in the establishment of the Hindu College in Calcutta in 1817, which later became Presidency College.

• His efforts in advocating for the abolition of sati led to the regulation banning the practice in 1829 by the British Governor-General, Lord William Bentinck.

• Atmiya Sabha:

• Founded in 1814, the Atmiya Sabha was an organization that aimed to discuss and propagate the ideas of monotheism and rationality.

• The Sabha's meetings involved discussions on the Upanishads, Vedas, and other scriptures to interpret them in a way that promoted a monotheistic view.

• It served as a platform for intellectuals to debate and discuss various social issues and the need for reforms in Hindu society.

• The Atmiya Sabha's activities laid the foundation for the later establishment of the Brahmo Samaj in 1828, which continued the reformist agenda.

• Brahmo Samaj:

• Founded by Raja Rammohun Roy in 1828, the Brahmo Samaj was a socio-religious reform movement that aimed to purify Hinduism and promote monotheism.

• The Brahmo Samaj sought to eliminate social evils such as caste discrimination, child marriage, and the dowry system.

• It emphasized the importance of education, especially for women, and supported widow remarriage.

• The movement had a significant impact on the Indian society and influenced many later reformers and movements.

• Social Reform in India:

• The early 19th century saw the emergence of several social reform movements in India aimed at addressing various social issues and promoting modernization.

• Reformers like Raja Rammohun Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Swami Vivekananda played crucial roles in advocating for change and improving the status of women and marginalized communities.

• These movements laid the groundwork for future social and political developments in India, including the struggle for independence.

• The reforms also contributed to the development of a more progressive and inclusive society in India.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is HCOOH.

Key Points

• HCOOH, also known as formic acid, is the simplest carboxylic acid and is the most acidic among the given options.

• Formic acid has the highest acidity due to the absence of electron-donating alkyl groups which decrease the acidity by destabilizing the conjugate base.

• The other options, such as C2H5COOH (propanoic acid), C3H7COOH (butanoic acid), and CH3COOH (acetic acid), have alkyl groups that reduce their acidity.

• Formic acid is widely used in various industrial processes and has a higher acid dissociation constant (Ka) compared to other carboxylic acids listed.

Additional Information

• Carboxylic Acids

• Carboxylic acids are organic acids characterized by the presence of a carboxyl group (–COOH).

• The acidity of carboxylic acids is due to the resonance stabilization of the carboxylate anion (R-COO−) formed after deprotonation.

• Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity by stabilizing the carboxylate anion, while electron-donating groups decrease acidity by destabilizing it.

• Acid Dissociation Constant (Ka)

• The acid dissociation constant (Ka) is a quantitative measure of the strength of an acid in solution.

• It is the equilibrium constant for the dissociation of an acid into its conjugate base and a proton (H⁺).

• Higher Ka values indicate stronger acids, as they dissociate more completely in solution.

• Formic acid has a higher Ka value compared to the other carboxylic acids listed, making it more acidic.

• Factors Influencing Acidity

• Inductive Effect: Electron-withdrawing groups increase acidity, while electron-donating groups decrease it.

• Resonance Effect: Resonance stabilization of the conjugate base increases acidity.

• Hybridization: Acidity increases with the s-character of the hybrid orbital holding the acidic hydrogen (sp > sp² > sp³).

• Solvation: Better solvation of the conjugate base in a solvent increases acidity.

Additional Information

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Nitric oxide.

Key Points

• Nitric oxide (NO) is not considered a greenhouse gas because it does not have a significant impact on the Earth's temperature or climate.

• Greenhouse gases are those that can absorb and emit infrared radiation, leading to the greenhouse effect. Nitric oxide does not significantly contribute to this process.

• Common greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O), all of which have a much higher potential to trap heat in the atmosphere.

• Nitric oxide is primarily known for its role in the formation of smog and its impact on the respiratory system, rather than its role as a greenhouse gas.

Additional Information

• Greenhouse Gases:

• Greenhouse gases are those gases in the Earth's atmosphere that trap heat. They allow sunlight to enter the atmosphere freely, but when the Earth's surface emits the energy back as infrared radiation (heat), greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit this radiation, warming the planet.

• The primary greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere are water vapor (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and ozone (O3).

• Human activities, such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes, have significantly increased the concentrations of these greenhouse gases, leading to global warming and climate change.

• Carbon Dioxide (CO2):

• Carbon dioxide is a colorless, odorless gas that is essential for plant life through the process of photosynthesis.

• It is produced by the combustion of fossil fuels, deforestation, and various industrial processes.

• CO2 is the most significant long-lived greenhouse gas in Earth's atmosphere, contributing to global warming and climate change.

• Methane (CH4):

• Methane is a potent greenhouse gas with a global warming potential many times greater than that of CO2 over a 20-year period.

• It is produced naturally through the decomposition of organic matter and human activities such as livestock farming, rice cultivation, and landfills.

• Despite its shorter atmospheric lifetime compared to CO2, methane's impact on global warming is substantial.

• Nitrous Oxide (N2O):

• Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas that is more effective than CO2 at trapping heat in the atmosphere over a 100-year period.

• It is emitted from agricultural and industrial activities, as well as during the combustion of fossil fuels and solid waste.

• N2O also plays a role in the depletion of the ozone layer in the stratosphere.

questions.q: Which allotrope of carbon was discovered by Robert F Curl, Harold W Kroto and Richard E Smalley in 1985?

Key Points

• Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon that was discovered by Robert F. Curl, Harold W. Kroto, and Richard E. Smalley in 1985.

• It consists of carbon atoms arranged in a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, or tube.

• Fullerenes are also known as "Buckyballs" because the first discovered fullerene (C₆₀) resembles the shape of a soccer ball.

• Fullerenes have unique properties that make them useful in materials science, electronics, and nanotechnology.

Additional Information

• Graphene:

• Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice.

• It is known for its remarkable electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties.

• Graphene is used in various applications, including electronics, composites, and energy storage.

• Lonsdaleite:

• Lonsdaleite, also known as hexagonal diamond, is an allotrope of carbon with a hexagonal lattice structure.

• It is formed under high-pressure conditions, typically during meteorite impacts.

• Lonsdaleite is harder than diamond and has potential applications in cutting and drilling tools.

• Carbophene:

• Carbophene is a less commonly known term and is not widely recognized in the scientific community.

• It may be a misnomer or an incorrect term for other carbon allotropes such as graphene or fullerenes.

questions.q: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?

• Annapurna Devi was an Indian surbahar (bass sitar) player of the Maihar gharana.

• Annapurna Devi was considered one of the foremost exponents of the surbahar, a rare and difficult instrument to master.

• She was also the spouse of the renowned sitar player Ravi Shankar and significantly contributed to the popularity of Indian classical music.

Additional Information

• The surbahar, also known as the bass sitar, is a plucked string instrument used in the Hindustani classical music of North India.

• It is often referred to as the "bass sitar" because it is larger than the sitar and has a lower pitch.

• The surbahar is designed for the elaborate, slow-tempo alap section of a raga performance, with its deep, resonant tones.

questions.q: In the year 1925, who extracted lipids from an erythrocyte sample and found that lipid monolayers are good for measuring molecular surface area versus lateral pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gorter and Grendel.

Key Points

• In 1925, Dutch scientists Evert Gorter and François Grendel conducted a groundbreaking experiment involving erythrocyte (red blood cell) lipid extraction.

• They found that the lipids extracted from erythrocytes could form a monolayer, which was pivotal in understanding the molecular surface area versus lateral pressure.

• Their work was fundamental in the development of the fluid mosaic model of cell membranes.

• Gorter and Grendel's experiment was one of the first to suggest that cell membranes are composed of a lipid bilayer.

Additional Information

• Lipid Monolayers and Bilayers:

• A lipid monolayer is a single layer of lipid molecules arranged on the surface of the water, with their hydrophobic tails in the air and hydrophilic heads in the water.

• A lipid bilayer is a double layer of lipids that form the fundamental structure of cell membranes, with hydrophobic tails facing inward and hydrophilic heads facing outward.

• These structures are crucial for maintaining the integrity and functionality of cell membranes.

• Erythrocytes (Red Blood Cells):

• Erythrocytes are the most common type of blood cell and are responsible for transporting oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues and carbon dioxide from the tissues back to the lungs.

• Their membrane composition and properties are essential for their deformability and functionality.

• Surface Area vs. Lateral Pressure:

• This concept involves measuring the surface area occupied by lipid molecules as a function of the lateral pressure applied to the monolayer.

• It is used to study the physical properties of lipid layers and understand cell membrane mechanics.

• Fluid Mosaic Model:

• Proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972, this model describes the cell membrane as a fluid combination of lipids and proteins.

• The lipids provide a flexible matrix, while proteins float in or on this lipid bilayer, contributing to various cellular functions.

II.Sales tax

III.MODVAT

IV.Service tax
questions.solution:
The correct answer is I, II, III, IV.

Key Points

• Land revenue was one of the oldest forms of taxation implemented during ancient and medieval periods.

• Sales tax was introduced much later as a form of indirect tax on the sale of goods.

• MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax) was introduced in 1986 to allow manufacturers to obtain credit for the excise duty paid on inputs.

• Service tax was introduced in 1994 as a tax levied on services provided.

Additional Information

• Land Revenue

• Land revenue is a tax or revenue imposed by the government on the ownership or use of land.

• It has been a major source of revenue for many governments historically, especially in agrarian societies.

• In India, during the British rule, land revenue was a significant component of colonial administration.

• Land revenue systems like the Zamindari, Ryotwari, and Mahalwari were implemented in different regions.

• Sales Tax

• Sales tax is a tax levied by the government on the sale of goods and services.

• It is generally a percentage of the sale price and is added to the total cost paid by the consumer.

• This form of tax is an important source of revenue for state governments.

• With the introduction of Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India in 2017, the sales tax regime was subsumed under GST.

• MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax)

• MODVAT was introduced in India in 1986.

• It allowed manufacturers to claim credit for the excise duty paid on inputs used in the production of goods.

• This system aimed to avoid the cascading effect of taxes and to make the tax structure more efficient.

• MODVAT was later replaced by CENVAT (Central Value Added Tax) and subsequently subsumed under GST.

• Service Tax

• Service tax was introduced in India in 1994.

• It was levied on specified services provided by service providers.

• Service tax was a part of the indirect tax regime and contributed significantly to the government’s revenue.

• With the advent of GST, service tax was abolished and integrated into the new tax structure.

questions.q: If x is an integer such that x + (1)/(x) = (65)/(8), then find the value of x - (1)/(x)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: x + 1/x = 65/8

Express 65/8 as a mixed fraction: 65/8 = 8 + 1/8

By comparing x + 1/x with 8 + 1/8, we can clearly see x = 8 or x = 1/8.

Since x is stated to be an integer, we take x = 8.

Therefore, x − 1/x = 8 − 1/8 = (64 − 1)/8 = 63/8.

∴ The correct answer is 63/8.

Alternate Method

Given:

x + 1/x = 65/8

x is an integer.

Calculation:

⇒ (x² + 1) / x = 65/8

By cross-multiplying, we get:

⇒ 8(x² + 1) = 65x

⇒ 8x² − 65x + 8 = 0

⇒ 8x² − 64x − x + 8 = 0

⇒ 8x(x − 8) − 1(x − 8) = 0

⇒ (8x − 1)(x − 8) = 0

⇒ x = 1/8 or x = 8

Since it is given that x is an integer, x = 8.

Now, we substitute x = 8 in the expression x − 1/x:

⇒ x − 1/x = 8 − 1/8

⇒ (64 − 1) / 8

⇒ 63/8

∴ The correct answer is 63/8.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identities for Reciprocals

The relationship between the sum and difference of a number and its reciprocal is given by: (x + 1/x)² − (x − 1/x)² = 4.

Nature of Roots in Quadratic Equations

questions.q: Arvind and Chetan started running simultaneously from the same point in the same direction on a circular track of length 210 m. If Arvind takes 180 seconds to complete one round, and Chetan takes 420 seconds to complete one round, after how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point on the track?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Time taken by Arvind to complete one round = 180 seconds = 3 minutes.

Time taken by Chetan to complete one round = 420 seconds = 7 minutes.

To find the time they meet for the first time at the starting point, we calculate the LCM of their individual lap times.

Meeting time = LCM(3, 7) = 21 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of circular track = 210 m

Time taken by Arvind (T₁) = 180 seconds

Time taken by Chetan (T₂) = 420 seconds



Formula Used:

Time to meet for the first time at the starting point = LCM of individual times taken to complete one round.

Calculations:

⇒ Prime factorization of 180 = 2² × 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM(180, 420) = 2² × 3² × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM(180, 420) = 4 × 9 × 5 × 7 = 1260 seconds

⇒ Convert total seconds into minutes = 1260 ÷ 60

⇒ Time to meet = 21 minutes

∴ The correct answer is 21 minutes.

Additional Information

Meeting First Time at Starting Point

When multiple people start from the same point simultaneously, they meet again at the starting point exactly at the LCM of the times taken by each to complete one full round independently.

Meeting First Time Anywhere on Track

If running in the same direction, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S₁ − S₂). If running in opposite directions, Time to meet = Track Length ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Number of Distinct Meeting Points

If the ratio of their speeds is a : b in its simplest form, they will meet at (a − b) distinct points if running in the same direction, and at (a + b) distinct points if running in opposite directions.

questions.q: If P is a digit such that 6954P is divisible by 11, then P equals:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the divisibility rule of 11 directly:

Sum of alternate digits (odd places) = 6 + 5 + P = 11 + P

Sum of remaining digits (even places) = 9 + 4 = 13

Difference = (11 + P) − 13 = P − 2

For divisibility by 11, P − 2 = 0 ⇒ P = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given:

A 5-digit number 6954P is exactly divisible by 11.

P is a single digit (0 to 9).

Method Used:

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of digits at odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th from right) = P + 5 + 6 = 11 + P

⇒ Sum of digits at even places (2nd, 4th from right) = 4 + 9 = 13

⇒ Difference = (11 + P) − 13

⇒ Difference = P − 2

⇒ For the difference to be a multiple of 11, the only possible value for a single digit P (0 ≤ P ≤ 9) is when the difference is exactly 0.

⇒ P − 2 = 0

⇒ P = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) if the sum of its digits is exactly divisible by 3 (or 9).

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Combined Divisibility Rule of 7, 11, and 13

Form alternating sums of blocks of three digits from right to left. If the resultant difference is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, then the original number is also divisible by 7, 11, or 13 respectively.

questions.q: In a bank, 6% interest is given on the deposited amount. The bank then invests the money in the stock market and is able to earn ₹30,000 for every ₹3,00,000. How much money is the bank earning finally if the total amount deposited in the bank is ₹60,00,000?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Bank's earning rate from the stock market = (30,000 ÷ 3,00,000) × 100 = 10%

Interest rate paid to depositors = 6%

Net profit margin for the bank = 10% − 6% = 4%

Final earnings of the bank = 4% of 60,00,000

Final earnings = (4 ÷ 100) × 60,00,000 = ₹2,40,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,40,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount deposited in the bank = ₹60,00,000

Interest given on deposited amount = 6%

Earnings from stock market = ₹30,000 for every ₹3,00,000



Calculations:

⇒ Total interest paid to depositors = 6% of ₹60,00,000

⇒ Total interest paid = (6 ÷ 100) × 60,00,000 = ₹3,60,000

⇒ Total money invested in the stock market by the bank = ₹60,00,000

⇒ Bank's total earnings from the market = (60,00,000 ÷ 3,00,000) × 30,000

⇒ Bank's total earnings = 20 × 30,000 = ₹6,00,000

⇒ Final earnings of the bank = Earnings from stock market − Interest paid to depositors

⇒ Final earnings = 6,00,000 − 3,60,000 = ₹2,40,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,40,000.

Additional Information

Return on Investment (ROI)

ROI is a performance measure used to evaluate the efficiency of an investment. Formula: ROI = (Net Profit ÷ Cost of Investment) × 100.

Net Yield / Margin

It represents the core difference between the rate an institution earns on investments and the rate it pays on its obligations. Net Margin = Earning Rate − Borrowing Rate.

When base values are uniform throughout the problem, percentages can be subtracted directly to calculate final absolute differences (e.g., 10% − 6% = 4% on the common base).

questions.q: A function of two variable varies directly with x and inversely with y. Determine function when x = 5 and y = 3. Given that, for x = 0 and y = 1, f = 15 and for x = 1 and y = 15, f = 2.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the function be a sum of direct and inverse variations: f = ax + b/y.

For x = 0, y = 1: f = 15 ⇒ a(0) + b/1 = 15 ⇒ b = 15.

For x = 1, y = 15: f = 2 ⇒ a(1) + 15/15 = 2 ⇒ a = 1.

The determined function is f = x + 15/y.

For x = 5 and y = 3: f = 5 + 15/3 = 5 + 5 = 10.

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

A function f(x, y) consists of two parts:

One part varies directly with x.

One part varies inversely with y.

f = 15 when x = 0 and y = 1.

f = 2 when x = 1 and y = 15.

Formula Used:

f = a × x + b ÷ y



Calculations:

⇒ Step 1: Substitute the first condition (x = 0, y = 1, f = 15) into the formula.

⇒ 15 = a × 0 + b ÷ 1

⇒ b = 15

⇒ Step 2: Substitute the second condition (x = 1, y = 15, f = 2) into the formula.

⇒ 2 = a × 1 + 15 ÷ 15

⇒ 2 = a + 1

⇒ a = 1

⇒ The complete function equation is f = x + 15/y.

⇒ Step 3: Find f when x = 5 and y = 3.

⇒ f = 5 + 15 ÷ 3

⇒ f = 5 + 5

⇒ f = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10.

Additional Information

Direct Variation

If two quantities A and B are in direct variation, they increase or decrease together proportionally. The equation takes the form A = k × B, where k is a constant.

Inverse Variation

If two quantities A and B are in inverse variation, an increase in one causes a proportional decrease in the other. The equation takes the form A = k ÷ B.

Partial Variation

When a value depends on the sum of two or more independent variables or conditions, it is expressed as a combined sum of multiple variations. Example: f = a × x + b ÷ y.

⇒ Perimeter = 31.6633 cm

Additional Information

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is given by A = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr². Alternatively, if the arc length l is known, the area can be directly calculated as A = (l × r) ÷ 2.

Length of a Circular Arc

The arc length represents the distance along the curved edge of the circle and is calculated as l = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Perimeter vs Arc Length

Students often confuse the perimeter of a sector with the arc length. The arc length is merely the curved boundary, while the full perimeter of the sector must include the two straight radii boundary lines, establishing the formula: Perimeter = l + 2r.

questions.q: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively, while a third pipe can empty it in 8 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill the empty tank if all three pipes are opened simultaneously?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Capacity (Total Work) = LCM(12, 18, 8) = 72 units.

Combined Efficiency = (72 ÷ 12) + (72 ÷ 18) − (72 ÷ 8)

⇒ 6 + 4 − 9 = 1 unit/hour.

Time required to fill the tank = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency = 72 ÷ 1 = 72 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 72 hours.

Alternate Method

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive efficiency), while an outlet pipe empties it (negative efficiency). The net efficiency of the system is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

Time and Work Concept
